findings.title: canManage() grants manage rights when only the VIEW scope is held
findings.body: `canManage()` (no-arg) falls back to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. An admin who has only `view` on the all-groups resource is therefore treated as able to manage groups. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` calls `auth.groups().requireManage()`, so a view-only admin can create top-level groups. The fallback should check only `MANAGE`. The new interface Javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` also says VIEW or MANAGE, which documents the wrong behaviour. The new tests do not catch this: none grants VIEW on all groups and then attempts a manage operation.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes and returns the resource UUID instead of the group id
findings.body: In the `findByType` callback, `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` is called and `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` is stored. In V2 the resource name is the group id: `getOrCreateResource` creates the resource with `name = group.getId()`, and `hasPermission` looks it up with `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. The resource's own UUID never matches a name, so `hasPermission` silently falls back to the all-groups type resource. The returned set also contains resource UUIDs rather than group ids. Consequences: `UsersResource`/`BruteForceUsersResource` set `UserModel.GROUPS` to ids that match no group, and `getUsersCount` is given the same wrong ids, so results can be empty or wrong. Per-group `view-members` permissions are never reflected in the id set. The new test only passes because the post-filter `canView(user)` hides the problem. The callback should use `getName()` for both the evaluation and the collected id.

findings.title: Possible NPE when the Groups type resource does not exist
findings.body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource(...)` returns null when the `Groups` resource is missing. The result is passed straight to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and then to `resource.getScopes()`. `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` returns early for realms that already have an admin-permissions client, so those realms never get the new `Groups` resource or the group scopes. For them every non-role-based group check would throw a NullPointerException (HTTP 500) instead of denying. There is no null guard and no migration.

findings.title: Javadoc of requireManageMembers and getGroupIdsWithViewPermission is wrong
findings.body: `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` is documented as throwing when `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false, but it delegates to `canManageMembers`. `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` says it returns a "Stream of IDs" but returns `Set<String>`. These are the new Javadocs this PR introduces for the interface, so they should be correct.

findings.title: getResourceName has no handling for the Groups resource type
findings.body: `getResourceName` special-cases only `USERS` ("All users" or the username). A Groups permission now falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Resources created by `getOrCreateResource` have no display name, and their name is the raw group id. Group permissions will therefore show a null or opaque UUID name instead of "All groups" or the group name.
